eyebrow: National organization · Bay and SF school vision services
program: Conditional whole-organization health value of a $100,000 unrestricted gift

nutshell.headline: School eyeglasses improve vision. The health value of the next unrestricted gift is less certain.
nutshell.body: Our conditional central estimate is $53.43 million per 10 SF-resident QALYs, $10.02 million for Bay residents including SF, and $801,000 nationally. These are explicit analyst judgments, not trial-measured QALYs or a priced funding offer. A favorable joint scenario passes $100,000 nationally but not for Bay or SF health.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Mobile examinations and glasses address real visual deficits; replacement-supported cohorts show sustained corrected vision. California donations may also enable federal financing.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Pediatric preference utility, care otherwise received, wearing time, gift allocation and marginal financing are not measured for the next gift.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: No verified marginal capacity, current complete cost quote, eligible matching headroom or pediatric QALY calibration.

summary.label: Central donor cost / 10 QALYs
summary.detail: The same gift produces .018716 SF, .099821 Bay and 1.247760 US QALYs. These are nested scopes, not additive.

summary.label: Whole gift
summary.detail: Central $80,000 clinical delivery and $20,000 shared institutional work; all costs retained, allocation judgmental.

summary.label: Recipient
summary.detail: Official provider disclosure; distinct from PHC adult glasses and PVF/Lions cataract care.

summary.label: Gross associated operating-resource envelope
summary.detail: Includes assumed donated delivery resources and failed/replaced provision; not net incremental full societal cost. Family time and some opportunity costs are omitted.

programSection.body: Vision To Learn provides school-based screenings, examinations, fitting and glasses to low-income children nationally, including SFUSD and other Bay districts. This ordinary-gift model represents that clinical core while retaining organizational overhead and unquantified work. Actual clinics are verified; modeled extra child-courses are not a capacity promise.

steps.title: Fund the whole organization
steps.detail: The core allocation funds complete delivery cash, including upstream screening and noncompletion. Shared administration, fundraising and other institutional work retain their cost.

steps.title: Enable additional care
steps.detail: Financial additionality distinguishes newly enabled courses from replacement funding; a separate clinical-gap prior excludes children already adequately corrected.

steps.title: Deliver and maintain useful glasses
steps.detail: Effective wearing time, not pair count, drives health. Second pairs and replacements preserve the same child's correction rather than create another health gain.

steps.title: Count finite health by residence
steps.detail: After an explicit dispensing delay, useful correction lasts only until the no-gift care comparator catches up. No lifetime learning, earnings or blindness-prevention tail is added.

programSection.boundary: Bay includes SF, within US. Regional resident shares are assumptions, not current output fractions. Overseas health is zero. Partner-provided care must not be counted again in another report.

model.headline: Finite corrected-vision time, not test scores converted into health
model.body: Central dispensing begins 1.5 months after donation and the incremental window lasts one year; favorable starts after one month for two years, pessimistic after three months for six months. All delays and catch-up times are judgments. Health is discounted at 3% from donation; shared service harm occurs at dispensing and independent donor harm at donation.

equation.label: Health for each base or matching tranche
equation.expression: Q = children × financial additionality × (uncorrected fraction × effective wear × utility × discounted corrected-time − shared harm), discounted to dispensing; apply tranche residence shares, then subtract independent donor harm.
equation.result: Central 1.247760 US QALYs / .099821 Bay / .018716 SF for the same $100,000.

inputs.label: Direct cash / associated in-kind per delivered child
inputs.basis: Complete direct-course allocation includes failed screens, exams, noncompletion and follow-up. Historical below-$150 provider narrative is not a current quote. Favorable $150 must support two years.

inputs.label: Clinical share of whole gift
inputs.basis: Remaining shared institutional costs retained; academic and broader benefits unquantified.

inputs.label: Financial additionality / uncorrected comparator
inputs.basis: Different funding and clinical substitutes; no third blanket replacement factor.

inputs.label: Effective correction fraction
inputs.basis: Includes loss and nonwear; not measured annual adherence or extra completion probability.

inputs.label: Preference utility while effectively corrected
inputs.basis: Unvalidated pediatric analyst prior. Chart-line and academic gains are not preference utility.

inputs.label: Ordinary base Bay / SF health shares
inputs.basis: Nested resident allocation priors, not measured marginal output. California match uses separate conditional Bay20% / SF3.75%.

inputs.label: New public matching cash
inputs.basis: An assumed1:1 match on40% California core budget only. Not an available donor offer or statutory rate.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Joint favorable inputs are not a verified offer or confidence bound. Null financial expansion or null clinical value produces no positive ratio; shared or independent health harm can make net QALYs negative. Independent harm geography uses ordinary resident-share priors, not a verified harm location. Zero dispensing delay reproduces v1 central for provenance.
model.fundingBoundary: Ordinary public reimbursement is baseline. Only the optional California match scenario adds NEW public cash, assuming eligibility, claims, capacity and a hypothetical rate. Base and match children have separate geography; the match does not fund non-California care. All public cash and in-kind allowances enter gross resource costs. Direct claims administration is assumed inside course cost; institutional capacity is not unlimited. This envelope counts committed failed/replaced provision and is not a net incremental societal CEA.

evidence.design: Guo et al.2021 cross-sectional presenting versus best-corrected acuity
evidence.result: 70% gained at least two better-eye chart lines on refraction.
evidence.transfer: Supports optical correction, not sustained wear, untreated delay or preference utility.

evidence.design: Mudie et al.2022 prospective school cohort
evidence.population: Baltimore second/third graders;206 at first follow-up
evidence.result: Presenting distance acuity improved from .14 to .05 logMAR; improvement persisted into the next school year.
evidence.transfer: Two pairs and replacement support were supplied. No randomized usual-care comparator; does not validate two-year delay avoided.

evidence.design: Neitzel et al.2021 randomized school rollout
evidence.result: Reading benefit at one year was not sustained at two years.
evidence.transfer: Academic effect is not converted to QALYs; its attenuation is not proof that visual benefit disappears.

evidence.design: Pediatric glasses-type QoL trial and adult economic evaluation
evidence.population: Chinese children and Indian adults, respectively
evidence.result: Pediatric NEI-RQL-42 is not preference utility; adult modeled utility is not validated US pediatric gain.
evidence.transfer: The model's0.02 utility remains an explicit analyst judgment.

evidence.result: VTL is a current provider; eligible private funding can draw federal CHIP funds.
evidence.transfer: No verified ordinary-gift match rate, headroom or new local slots. Existing reimbursement is not automatically incremental.

reservations: Utility, adherence, clinical catch-up, marginal costs and regional shares are weakly calibrated judgments.
Two-year favorable correction requires replacement and follow-up within a low assumed cash budget.
Current Baltimore replacement copy inconsistently states18months versus one year; no national guarantee inferred.
Public reimbursement, donated glasses and public screening require partner-resource accounting and substitution checks.
Do not add school test-score gains, referrals, two pairs per child or partner counts as separate QALYs.
excludedBenefits: Unproven lifetime amblyopia or blindness prevention
